    ABOUT TRANSITSENSE

    An IoT framework for safer, smoother city streets.

    The problem

    Blind junctions cause collisions, ambulances lose minutes at red lights, cities rarely know what traffic actually uses their roads, and drivers circle looking for parking. Each of these is a sensing problem: the information exists, but nobody measures it in time.

    Our solution

    • Junction warning · a LiDAR post sees cars approaching a blind corner and turns the other approaches red.
    • Ambulance priority · two microphones locate a siren, and the signals clear and hold green for it.
    • Magnetic counting · a magnetometer in the road counts and classifies every vehicle.
    • Predictive parking · zone cameras track bays and predict the bay that will be free when you arrive.

    How the hardware works

    Each system runs on an ESP32 microcontroller with low-cost sensors: a TFmini-S LiDAR, two INMP441 microphones, a QMC5883L magnetometer and an ESP32-CAM. All four also run together on one ESP32 in the Wokwi simulator, which sends every event over Wi-Fi and MQTT to this website within about a second. The website can send commands back, for example to flash the lights in Wokwi.

    Click any sensor label marked i in the city for its parts, wiring and Arduino code.

    EXPLORE TRANSITSENSE

    Four sensors. One connected city.

    Pick a sensor from the bar below, then press its action button to watch the city respond in real time.

    • Move around — drag to orbit; scroll or pinch to zoom. Right-drag to pan.
    • Keyboard — use + / − to zoom and 0 to reset the camera. Space pauses the simulation.
    • Real hardware — click a sensor label marked i in the city, or “Hardware & code” in the panel, to see the ESP32 parts, wiring and Arduino code.
    • Sound — the ambulance siren plays through your speakers. Use the speaker button at the top to mute it.
    • Try edge cases — test a departing car, a sensor fault, or a reflected siren.

    All traffic, sensor readings, classifications, and parking forecasts are simulated. This showcase uses no microphone, camera, or real-world data.
